title: Carl Jefferson and the Concord Jazz Festival hospitality
summary: Royal praises Carl Jefferson, the royalty deals, the car sold at cost, and the amphitheater's lavish treatment of musicians.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, Jefferson is a very nice man. It's a pleasure to work for Carl, because he's a very sincere man and he's not trying to collect all the potatoes. He gives -- he probably gives the musicians that record with him a better deal than anybody else in recording business, so far as the royalty deal because that's not his thing. He's doing it out of love, really, I think, because he loves jazz. He happens to be the owner of the largest distribution for Lincoln-Mercury cars in the Bay Area and so that is actually his business. So, this other is just a thing on the side that he does because he loves jazz. He loves this Concord Jazz Festival and he's done a wonderful job on an (unintelligible.). As a matter of fact, he was so very nice that he ended up selling me a car in '77, a very beautiful car, at complete cost.
And you can't beat that for a friend, because nobody gives you anything now at cost. He was a very

That's great. I know Bill Berry has mentioned how nice Carl Jefferson is. He treats artists as artists would like to be treated. He said he asks nothing of you except that you give your very best performance and he said he makes you feel like wanting to.

He just wants you to give a performance and on top of that, he built this very fine amphitheater, a building that he really got out and really drummed up a whole lot of money to get it built and it's one of the only places where musicians play, where they have adequate rest dressing rooms and facilities for the actual working performer. On top of that, everytime you go out of your room, there's a washtub full of soft drinks and beer for you to get. He keeps smorgas-bord and all sorts of sandwiches and fruits and everything, to just make you happy at all times, which you do not find in the music and entertainment business anywhere.
Yeah, Bill says he even has somebody who meets -- has someone to meet your plane?

He meets you at the plane with a fleet of brand new Continentals, usually, air-conditioned, and you drive there and all during the time in between your motels, which he picks up the rent for, going in between, he has liveried drivers driving you to and from work, with some sort of Lincoln-Mercury product.
That's a nice piece of public relations.

Yeah, Bill told me all that when I interviewed him for Downbeat and I put it in a story (inaudible) and Downbeat cut out all reference to Carl ________ and I was kind of surprised. It's kind of too bad. Somebody like that deserves some credit for what he's doing, I believe.
